findings.comment: Building locations shown on site plan with overhead electric line on southern boundary. No building elevation sheets provided showing surveyed conductor elevations or roof/eave elevations. Cannot verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained without these essential elevation views and dimension callouts.

applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings relative to southern overhead line
findings.comment: Overhead electric line documented on southern boundary. Building locations shown but no clearance dimensions provided. Cannot verify 15-foot radial clearance without dimension callouts, conductor identification (primary/secondary/neutral), and voltage specifications.

No building elevation sheets provided showing projections (overhangs, eaves, balconies, roofs, patios). Cannot verify required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from building projections without elevation views.

applicableAreas: Northern property boundary where overhead utilities exist on adjacent property and site
findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents overhead utility line on-site along northern property boundary. Proposed site plan (Sheet 9) omits northern overhead utilities with no demolition, relocation, or undergrounding notes. Cannot verify building setbacks from ROW and relocated facilities when existing utilities are not accounted for in proposed plan.

No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan set showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations or clearance dimensions to building faces and projections. This is a critical missing document type explicitly required by code to demonstrate vertical clearances from overhead electric conductors are met.

applicableAreas: All 8 proposed buildings relative to overhead lines
findings.comment: No section or profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to building edges, projections, or other site features. Plans show buildings and overhead lines in plan view only with no cross-section documentation of vertical and horizontal relationships or clearance dimensions.

applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing southern property boundary where overhead electric line exists
findings.comment: Site plan shows proposed driveways crossing under overhead electric line on southern boundary. No vertical clearance dimensions provided on grading plan, profile sections, or utility plan. No determination whether truck traffic applies (16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement). No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data provided. Cannot verify driveways maintain minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead facilities including any telecommunications attachments.

applicableAreas: Northern property boundary where utility pole exists on existing conditions survey
findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents overhead utility pole on-site along northern property boundary. Proposed site plan (Sheet 9) omits this pole location with no notation regarding relocation, removal, or disposition. If pole remains and any site improvements (driveway, building, etc.) are within 30 feet of pole, relocation to minimum 30 feet from driveway edge is required. Current plan does not address pole conflicts.

applicableAreas: All clearance dimensions throughout site plan where overhead utilities exist
findings.comment: Plans show overhead lines but provide no clearance dimension callouts measuring distances from features to overhead conductors. Code requires clearance dimensions extend from outside conductor (not pole centerline or centerline of multi-conductor lines), yet no dimensions are provided to verify this measurement methodology. Cannot verify compliance when dimensions are completely absent.

applicableAreas: Proposed buildings and driveways crossing overhead electric distribution facilities on southern boundary
findings.comment: Code establishes absolute prohibition against installing customer facilities (buildings, driveways, structures) under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, independent of clearance distances. Plans show driveways crossing under southern overhead line and buildings near overhead facilities. No explicit documentation confirms facilities are not placed directly beneath/over conductors. Cannot confirm compliance with absolute prohibition.

applicableAreas: All buildings and driveways where vertical clearance from overhead facilities appears marginal
findings.comment: Building finished floor elevations range 686.25-685 ft MSL; overhead conductor elevations unknown. Without surveyed conductor heights and building roof elevations, vertical clearances cannot be verified and appear marginal. Code requires registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey and site-specific analysis when vertical clearance requirements may not be met. This critical survey and analysis are not provided despite marginal clearance conditions.

applicableAreas: Proposed mitigation trees on southern property area within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) depicts proposed mitigation trees approximately 10-15 feet from southern overhead electric line. Code requires trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors be Utility Compatible species per ECM Appendix F (UC designation, generally mature height ≤20 feet). Specific tree species not confirmed on landscape plan. Cannot verify proposed trees are utility-compatible; if non-compatible species are planted, they will grow into overhead conductors, creating safety hazard.

applicableAreas: Utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries
findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries. Down guy wires and anchor locations are typically omitted from plans but are critical infrastructure. Site plan does not show any down guy wires, anchors, or associated clearances. If poles have down guys (common for distribution poles) and site improvements (driveways, accessible paths, buildings) are located near pole bases, guy anchors and cables could conflict with these features. Requires verification from Austin Energy and survey documentation.

applicableAreas: Utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries if down guys are present
findings.comment: Easement exhibit (Sheet 2) and site plan do not show down guy anchor easements. Per Austin Energy transmission engineering standards, down guy anchors from distribution poles require dedicated 10-foot-wide easement extending minimum 5 feet past anchor ground entry point. If poles have down guys (typical for poles on property), required easements must be depicted on plat and easement exhibits. Missing easement documentation represents deficiency.

No construction logistics, staging plan, or equipment operation zones provided on site plans. Code requires construction staging areas, equipment laydown zones, and work platforms maintain minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333 and UCM § 1.10.2. This is mandatory separate requirement from permanent clearances. Plans must include logistics plan or note addressing construction phase clearances from overhead lines.

Cover sheet and general notes do not include required notification regarding high-voltage work. Code requires plans to include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before any work begins near high-voltage overhead lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. This safety notification is mandatory when overhead electric facilities exist on or adjacent to site and construction is proposed.
